title: Natural England objected to a datacentre. Weeks later ministers threatened to abolish the agency

title: GTA in Istanbul? Meet the game developers bringing virtual crime chaos to their home cities
summary: From Helsinki to Istanbul, independent developers are putting Grand Theft Auto-style action on their home streets, and without billion-dollar budgets. They tell us how they do it Like most kids who shouldn’t have been playing Grand Theft Auto III in 2001, Eamonn Swayah imagined a version of Rockstar Games’ groundbreaking criminal sandbox set in his own back yard. In his case, that was a Manchester council estate, complete with local accents, driving on the left, and plenty of ways to hustle. He didn’t know it, but swapping the game’s facsimile of early 2000s New York City for a different setting was an idea he shared with many watchful game developers. Rockstar’s 3D open world template, it turned out, could be plonked in just about any location, so long as it had people and enough cars to run them over with. After GTA III attracted immense commercial success (and controversy), dozens of copycats and spiritual sequels hit the market throughout the 00s and 2010s. Gamers had a pithy name for them: “GTA clones”. Continue reading...

title: It’s the biggest ever month for video games – so why am I playing a title from 2006? | Dominik Diamond
summary: While everyone else is giddy over Zelda and GTA, Dominik Diamond finds himself behind the times on a Nintendo Wii I find myself on the wrong side of gaming history this month. I have zero zeitgeist. My takes are as fresh as something found at the rear of the fridge. I haven’t even played Grand Theft Auto VI yet, but we’ll get to that. Worse, all month, the Nintendo sector of the gaming world has been going googly eyed over Zelda. The Ocarina of Time remake seems to have produced more joy than all the puppies in the world. But not for me. I have never liked Zelda. It’s like being a movie reviewer who doesn’t like Disney, or a vegan shark. Continue reading...

title: The Com: the global cybercrime network posing a ‘chilling threat’ to children
summary: FBI estimates thousands of people identify as members, or recent members, of group linked to indecent images of girls and blackmail It sounds benign: the Com, short for the Community. But crime agencies around the world warn that it is far from that and the young cybercriminals involved are causing havoc and putting children at chilling, sickening risk. Beau-Jack Mensforth was jailed by a UK judge on Friday for his activities as part of the Com. He was one individual operating from his bedroom in north-east England, but there are probably thousands more like him and parents are being urged by police to be aware and to check their children’s devices. title: The best cordless vacuum cleaners for a spotless home: 10 tried and tested favourites
summary: Stick vacuums are a convenient alternative to corded designs, but which model wins for overall cleaning prowess? Our expert reveals all • The best robot vacuums • How to make your vacuum last longer Choosing a cordless vacuum is a big decision. Whichever model you go for, you’re likely to use it for years, relying on its ability to suck up dust, crumbs, mud, pet hair and any other dry spillages or sheddings. Choosing the right model can be the difference between an effective cleaner that’s a delight to pull out of the cupboard and a dud that you dread having to unblock, detangle and clean after every use. In this review, I took 18 of the leading cordless vacuum cleaners from a range of manufacturers and at various prices and inflicted the same cleaning tests on each one.
